questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows:

"On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court delivered a sensational verdict unseating Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, finding her guilty of electoral malpractices in Rae Bareli. On 24 June, Supreme Court vacation judge Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer granted only a conditional stay. Faced with calls for her resignation, on the night of 25 June 1975, Indira Gandhi advised President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a National Emergency under Article 352 on the subjective grounds of 'internal disturbance'. Before the Union Cabinet was even informed, electricity to major newspaper printing presses in Delhi was severed, and top opposition leaders—including JP, Morarji Desai, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee—were arrested under MISA. Fundamental rights were suspended, strict press censorship was imposed, and extra-constitutional power was wielded by Sanjay Gandhi, who enforced ruthless slum demolitions at Turkman Gate and coercive sterilization quotas. In April 1976, in the infamous ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (Habeas Corpus) case, the Supreme Court four-judge majority disgracefully ruled that citizens could not approach courts for protection of life or liberty during Emergency. Only Justice H.R. Khanna courageously dissented, defending inviolable human liberty."

"By 1973–1974, popular disenchantment with the Indira Gandhi government reached boiling point amidst runaway inflation (nearly 30%), food shortages, rising unemployment, and pervasive corruption. In March 1974, students in Bihar rose in protest against unemployment and corruption. NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 6: The Crisis of Democratic Order): (A) In March 1974, students in Bihar came together in protest against rising prices and corruption, inviting Jayaprakash Narayan to lead the movement (Match III). (B) The National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen's Struggle led by George Fernandes staged a 20-day nationwide strike in May 1974 (Match IV). (C) The Supreme Court delivered the historic Kesavananda Bharati verdict in April 1973 (Match I). (D) Emergency was declared on the night of 25 June 1975 (Match II). Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText:
Arrange the following political developments in the correct chronological
order.
 
(A) The National Coordination Committee of Railwaymen's Struggle gave a
call for a nation-wide strike.
(B) Massive demonstration organized by Jayaprakash Narayan in Delhi's
Ramlila grounds.
(C) The government set aside the seniority of three judges and appointed
A.N. Ray as the Chief Justice of India.
(D) Shah Commission of Inquiry was appointed.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Chronology: (C) In April 1973, Justice A.N. Ray was appointed CJI, superseding three senior judges; (A) In May 1974, George Fernandes led the nationwide railway strike; (B) On 25 June 1975, Jayaprakash Narayan addressed a mammoth rally at Ramlila Ground calling for civil disobedience; (D) In May 1977, the Janata government appointed the Shah Commission of Inquiry. Sequence: (C), (A), (B), (D).
Hence, option (A) is correct.
